c.tagline: Ireland's rebel city — a foodie harbour town of pubs, bells and Georgian charm.

taxi.fareNote: There is no private ride-share in Ireland — Uber operates only as a licensed-taxi dispatcher. Hail on the street, use a rank, or book via the FreeNow app; metered fares are set by national regulation.

emergency.note: 112 (EU-wide) and 999 both connect to Garda (police), ambulance, fire, and coast guard.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Shandon: Shandon Bells and St Anne's Church, Cork

avoid.reason: Usual late-night pub-crowd awareness around St Patrick's Street and Oliver Plunkett Street at weekend closing time.

hood_desc: The compact island city centre between the two channels of the River Lee, home to St Patrick's Street, the covered English Market, Grand Parade and the main shops; the walkable base where most first-timers stay.

The historic north-side hill district crowned by the Shandon Bells and St Anne's Church, with the old Butter Exchange, Firkin Crane and steep lanes of pastel houses; steeped in sightseeing and local character.

The revived MacCurtain Street strip on the near north bank, Cork's 'Victorian Quarter' of independent restaurants, cocktail bars, music venues and boutique hotels; the heart of the city's going-out scene.

A leafy southside suburb around Douglas Village and its shopping centres, with quiet residential streets and easy access to the coast road; popular with families and longer-stay visitors wanting calm.
The elegant tree-lined avenue running west past University College Cork, Fitzgerald Park and the Cork Public Museum, dotted with Georgian guesthouses; a genteel, green base near the university.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 11:30 PM, with limited NiteLink services on weekends; commuter trains run from early morning to late evening.
transit.note: Cork has no metro or tram; getting around means Bus Éireann city buses and the Cork commuter rail lines out of Kent Station, plus a very walkable compact centre.
transit.pay: Tap on with a Leap Card or contactless bank card; cash is accepted on buses (exact fare preferred). Leap Cards give cheaper capped fares.

sys.n: Cork Commuter Rail (Cobh / Midleton / Mallow lines)

bus: Aircoach & GoBus intercity coaches to Dublin

car.idp: Not required for EU/UK licences; recommended for others

train: Cork commuter rail to Cobh & Midleton (Kent Station)

transit.m: Bus Éireann route 226 to city centre (~25-30 min, frequent)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up the bill or leaving ~10% for good table service in restaurants is appreciated.
